title: LETTER 5: Letter from Bank to Loan Defaulter — Recovery Notice

blocks.content: Topic: You are a Branch Manager. Write a formal letter to Mr. Ramesh Kumar, who has not repaid his personal loan for 75 days, requesting him to regularise the account immediately.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A loan recovery notice is a formal communication sent by a bank to a borrower defaulting on loan installments.
The letter must clearly mention account details, outstanding dues, overdue principal, interest accrued, and a firm deadline for payment.
Account default exceeding 90 days leads to classification as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) under RBI guidelines.
Failure to clear dues within the specified timeline empowers the bank to initiate legal proceedings under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 or Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRT).
In descriptive writing exams, maintaining a professional, assertive, yet legally complaint tone is critical for scoring high marks.

blocks.content: Failure to clear the outstanding dues within 15 days will compel the bank to initiate legal proceedings under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 for recovery of the loan.
Subject: Final Reminder for Regularisation of Personal Loan Account No. PLAL-7834521 — Urgent Action Required

rows: Account classified as NPA (90+ days overdue)
Remind borrower and encourage voluntary settlement
Pre-requisite step before enforcing security interest/seizure

blocks.content: We refer to your Personal Loan Account No. PLAL-7834521 sanctioned by our branch on 15 June 2024 for an amount of Rs. 3,50,000 at an interest rate of 12.5% per annum, repayable in 36 monthly instalments. We write to bring to your immediate notice that as of this date, your account has an outstanding overdue of Rs. 29,450, comprising three EMIs that have remained unpaid since 25 December 2024 — a period of 75 days.

As per the terms of your loan agreement and the Reserve Bank of India's prudential norms, a borrowal account where principal or interest remains overdue for more than 90 days is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA). We wish to inform you that your account will be reported as NPA to the credit bureaus (CIBIL, Equifax, CRIF HighMark) within the next 15 days unless all outstanding dues are cleared in full.

Classification as NPA will severely damage your credit score, restricting your ability to obtain any loans or credit cards in the future. You are therefore requested to deposit the outstanding amount of Rs. 29,450, along with applicable penal charges, at the earliest and not later than 10 April 2025.

Should you be facing temporary financial hardship, we invite you to contact our branch for exploring the possibility of loan restructuring or a repayment reschedulement. Please treat this as a final reminder before regulatory and legal recovery measures are initiated.

items: Always include mandatory elements: Loan Account Number, Total Overdue Amount, Specific Deadline Date, and Consequences of Non-Payment.
Ensure formal letter format: Sender Address (Bank Manager), Date, Receiver Address (Borrower), Subject Line, Salutation, Body, and Formal Sign-off.
Avoid informal or aggressive language; stick to official banking terminology and regulatory compliance language.

blocks.content: Punjab National Bank, Civil Lines Branch

Examiner's Tip: Recovery letters must be firm but not threatening. Mention regulatory consequences (NPA classification, CIBIL impact) factually. Always offer a pathway to resolution. This demonstrates both legal knowledge and empathy.
